# delivery-quality: what it prints

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_demos.py from real runs; do not edit by
     hand. CI fails when this file no longer matches the code. -->

Real output of [delivery-quality](../../plugins/delivery-quality) on the fixtures its own
tests use. Skills and subagents are not shown: what they say depends on the
model, and they are measured by the eval cases in the plugin's `evals/`.

## guard_destructive stops a history rewrite on main

The hook reads the Bash call before it runs. Exit 2 blocks it and hands the message to Claude, which is how the model learns what to do instead.

Input:

```json
{
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": {
    "command": "git push origin main --force"
  },
  "cwd": "/home/user/app"
}
```

```console
$ python3 plugins/delivery-quality/scripts/guard_destructive.py < plugins/delivery-quality/tests/fixtures/destr-force-push-main.json
Blocked by guard_destructive: Force-pushing to main rewrites history other people have already pulled; --force-with-lease rewrites it too, so it is not an alternative.
Push to a new branch instead (git push -u origin HEAD:main-rewrite) and tell the user; if main itself must be rewritten, ask the user to do it.
[exit 2]
```

## guard_secrets blocks a key on a command line

The value is masked in the message, so the block does not repeat the leak it prevented.

Input:

```json
{
  "tool_name": "Bash",
  "tool_input": {
    "command": "aws configure set aws_access_key_id AKIA4TQ7XZ2PLMN8DKQV"
  }
}
```

```console
$ python3 plugins/delivery-quality/scripts/guard_secrets.py < plugins/delivery-quality/tests/fixtures/secret-aws-key.json
Blocked by guard_secrets: this command line contains a string shaped like a real AWS access key id (AKIA4T…QV). Nothing was written.
Do not retry with the value split, encoded or moved to another file; that still puts the secret on disk.
- Writing or passing it: don't. Reference an environment variable the user has set ($NAME) and ask them to set it if it is missing.
- Looking for where it leaked: search for the pattern, not the value, e.g. grep -rnE 'AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}' .
- The user says this exact string must be kept: stop and ask them to add the exception themselves.
[exit 2]
```
